>MOTHERBOARD
Avoid ASRock AM5 boards, CPU degradation issues still reported
Choose boards with ALC1220 audio codec when possible

>RAM
Crucial RAM & SSD warranty offers refunds only, no replacements
DDR5: 2x16GB or 2x24GB, 6000CL30 (AMD), 6400CL32 (Intel)
Workstation: 2x 32GB (budget), 2x48GB or 2x64GB (high-end)
DDR4: 3200CL16, 3600CL18

>SSD (update firmware)
DRAMless: (SN)7100, C925G, NM790
PCIe Gen 4.0: (SN)850X
Gen 5.0: (SN)8100

>GPU
Buy the best one you're willing to pay for

Budget: 165/180Hz IPS (24" 1080p / 27" 1440p)

High-end: wait for 2027 OLED releases
Check reviews & owner feedback

>CASE FANS

item.title: [ 31] /napt/ AI Pokemon Thread #282: Tired Doctor's Gigantic Hands Edition
item.description:
Previously on /napt/:

>>59647343

This is a general thread for people to post their AI art and/or make requests from others who may want to attempt making their own Pokémon-related gens.

Local Generation is the best option, requires a video card. Guides for local genning can be found in the /g/ threads:
https://rentry.org/comfyui_guide_1girl
>>>/g/ldg
Other Stable Diffusion threads are on: /h/, /e/, /d/, /b/, /vt/, /aco/, /trash/

NovelAI v4.5 is a paid AI generator. Opus tier users have "unlimited" Small/Normal generations, though editing tools require credits.

Midjourney is a paid AI generator, also capable of video. Usage requires a monthly subscription, with basically infinite gens.

Microsoft's Bing AI is a free image generator that is powered by DALL·E 3.

Civitai is free using its ‘buzz’ currency. You get a certain amount every day, plus more for liking models and gens.
>civitai.com

Otaiku is a (mostly) free mobile app. An ad watch is required between each image generation unless you pay.
>ailla.biz/otaiku
free video generation
>videomaker.me/app

Tensor is another generator that gives free daily credits, as well as a vast library of LoRAs to train your prompts on. Subscriptions are available for those who wish to pursue more than this.
>https://tensor.art/

Pastebin of Pokémon artists:
>https://pastebin.com/U0mmK3Tm

Characters with under 50 images will require more tags to have them look correct. This is a list of all Pokémon characters with over 300 images:
>https://danbooru.donmai.us/posts?tags=*_%28pokemon%29+&z=5

[Multiple images to share? Conserve space. Either collage or catbox them.]

[NO grotesque or violent images. If you really wanna share those, catbox them.]

A message from ThatOneAIAnon:
>Heya, fellow /napts, I've updated the Novelai artist tool to 4.5, and added an ELO ranking system so you can rank your favorite artists more easily

WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gasoline and many other goods and services became more expensive, evidence that rising prices remain an economic challenge just a few weeks before midterm elections that have focused heavily on affordability.

The consumer price index rose 3.7% in September compared with a year ago, the Labor Department said Wednesday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, costs jumped 0.6% from August to September, the biggest gain in five months, up from a 0.4% increase the previous month.

The figures underscore the lingering impact of the Iran war on gas prices and the stubborn persistence of inflation, which has ticked higher since the war began in late February. The rise isn’t all linked to oil and gas, as surging investment in data centers and AI has also pushed up prices for computer chips and the consumer electronics that use them. Elevated inflation has posed political problems for Republicans in Congress and is a challenge for the Federal Reserve, which is required by Congress to seek stable prices.

Excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 2.6% in September from a year ago, up from 2.4% the previous month and higher than economists had expected. And they climbed 0.3% from August to September, an elevated pace that, if it continued for a year, would run well above the Fed’s 2% target.

Higher inflation will likely put more pressure on the Fed to lift its key interest rate at its next meeting Oct. 27-28. Economists noted that the report showed price increases were spread more broadly across the economy than in recent months.

As President Donald Trump and his administration have ratcheted up pressure on Ukraine to stop striking Russian refineries, citing harm to American consumers, they have remained silent on recent Russian strikes on US businesses in Ukraine.

Russia has escalated its attacks on facilities tied to American corporations – and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine writ large – over the past several months.

According to Andy Hunder, the President of the American Chamber of Commerce in Ukraine, Russian missiles and drones have damaged facilities belonging to some of America’s most notable brands, including Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, McDonalds and Oreo.

Although Russia has tried to deter successful American business in the past, it’s “nothing we’ve seen like over the last months,” Hunder told CNN.

“This is a direct hit with drones and missiles, and they keep hitting them. It’s sending a message that they’re targeting American business. We’re not seeing any response from the White House,” he said.

“We need this to stop because these are American interests, American money, American investors that are being hit and are being targeted,” he said.

When a Russia drone struck a Coca-Cola factory outside Kyiv in early September, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attack was a “clear signal” to the US.

“Today, the Russians struck a Coca-Cola plant with a drone. Coca-Cola has become such an enemy to them that they’re burning it down with their Shaheds,” Zelensky said in his nightly video address on September 3, referring to “Iranian-designed drones.”

item.title: [101] Liberals cheer on illegal attacks on GOP Propaganda sources
item.description:
UKRAINE is INTERFERING in US elections by ILLEGALLY aiding democrats by ATTACKING data centers owned by GOP allies ahead of the november election.

https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/russian-disinformation-bot-traffic-nearly-eliminated-overnight-after-ukraine-drone-strikes-cripple-multiple-of-russias-google-data-centers-ukraine-intensifies-bombing-of-yandex-data-centers-in-response-to-moscows-strikes-on-kyiv-data-centers

Russian bot traffic has dropped dramatically in the past few days after Ukraine knocked out Yandex’s biggest data centers, with a third attack happening last night. Cloudflare reports that bot traffic from the Yandex network has dropped to just 0.4% of the maximum number of HTTP requests recorded in the past two weeks. It initially dropped to around 57% on Oct. 8, which happened when Ukraine hit a Yandex data center housing two supercomputers in Sasovo, Russia, located around 195 miles to the southeast of the Kremlin. A second, bigger Yandex campus in Kaluga, about 220 miles to the west of Sasovo, was knocked offline yesterday.

These attacks are apparently Ukraine’s response to Moscow’s strikes on its own data centers, some of which resulted in the outage of some of the most popular piracy websites.

Yandex is Russia’s equivalent to Google, and its Yandex Cloud service status reports that at least 84 services are currently offline. Global internet monitoring firm NetBlocks said that Yandex’s network traffic has dropped to just 30% for Yandex Cloud and 63% for Yandex LLC, most likely resulting in slower internet services or complete disruption for the average Russian. Unfortunately, the ordinary Russian wouldn’t be able to use high-speed satellite internet as a backup, as Starlink does not work in Russia, while the competing Rassvet constellation has had a good number of its existing satellites fall back to the surface after launch.

People and animals (and at least one tree) are changing at random in their sleep, waking up still in the real world, but now as Pokemon, and nobody knows why (that includes you.
